sentences.zh: 本周，我们为您带来一期往期节目。

sentences.en: Maybe more than any other Hidden Brain episode, this one brings a smile to our faces.
sentences.zh: 或许比《隐藏的大脑》任何其他节目都更能让我们会心一笑。

sentences.en: And right now, that's something we can all use.
sentences.zh: 而此时此刻，这正是我们大家都需要的。

sentences.zh: 节目开始。

sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: When Sophie Scott was about six, she came across her parents doing something very strange.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·斯科特大约六岁时，偶然撞见父母在做一件非常奇怪的事。

sentences.en: They were rolling around, laughing.
sentences.zh: 他们在地上打滚，大笑不止。

sentences.en: In my memory, they were actually on the floor of the living room, absolutely overcome with laughter.
sentences.zh: 在我的记忆里，他们当时就在客厅地板上，完全被笑声淹没了。

sentences.en: They'd laughed so much, they could literally do nothing else but laugh.
sentences.zh: 他们笑得太厉害了，除了笑，什么也做不了。

sentences.en: What had got them laughing was a song.
sentences.zh: 让他们笑个不停的是一首歌。

sentences.en: A comedy song about what people were not supposed to do in toilets on trains.
sentences.zh: 一首关于人们在火车厕所里不该做什么的滑稽歌曲。

sentences.en: It's set to quite a famous piece of music, and it goes,
sentences.zh: 它配上一段相当著名的音乐，歌词是这样的：

sentences.en: Customers will please refrain from passing water while the train is in the station, darling, I love you.
sentences.zh: 亲爱的，当火车停靠站台时，请各位乘客切勿排泄，我爱你。

sentences.en: We encourage constipation while the train is in the station.
sentences.zh: 我们鼓励在火车停靠站台时保持便秘。

sentences.en: And as they remembered more and more of it, they got more and more helpless.
sentences.zh: 随着他们记起的歌词越来越多，他们也越来越无法自拔。

sentences.en: Some water, kindly call up the water.
sentences.zh: 有些水，请呼叫水。

sentences.en: You'll place a vessel in the vessel.
sentences.zh: 你会把容器放在容器里。

sentences.en: Now maybe you're thinking, wait, this song isn't that funny.
sentences.zh: 现在你可能在想，等等，这首歌没那么好笑吧。

sentences.en: Try the platform in the rear.
sentences.zh: 试试后面的站台。

sentences.en: But we've all been there, right?
sentences.zh: 但我们都有过这种经历，对吧？

sentences.en: You're with a friend, they say something ridiculous, and then your laughter triggers their laughter.
sentences.zh: 你和朋友在一起，他们说了句荒唐的话，然后你的笑声又引发了他们的笑声。

sentences.en: Sophie didn't know then that laughter would play a big role in her life.
sentences.zh: 苏菲当时并不知道笑声会在她的人生中扮演如此重要的角色。

sentences.en: But today, she thinks about laughter a lot.
sentences.zh: 但今天，她经常思考笑声。

sentences.en: She's a neuroscientist who studies the science of laughter.
sentences.zh: 她是一位研究笑声科学的神经科学家。

sentences.en: So she often thinks back to that moment with her parents, back when she was six.
sentences.zh: 所以她经常回想起六岁时与父母在一起的那个时刻。

sentences.en: Years and years later, my father was mortally ill.
sentences.zh: 多年以后，我父亲病危了。

sentences.en: I mean, he thought he was dying.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他以为自己快不行了。

sentences.en: We all thought he was dying.
sentences.zh: 我们也都以为他快不行了。

sentences.en: And the doctors didn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 医生们束手无策。

sentences.en: And we were just sitting around waiting for something to happen.
sentences.zh: 我们只是坐在那里，等待着什么发生。

sentences.en: And my father suddenly said, we've laughed a lot, haven't we?
sentences.zh: 我父亲突然说：“我们笑过很多次，不是吗？”

sentences.en: And I said, yes, we have.
sentences.zh: 我说：“是的，我们笑过。”

sentences.en: And I thought, you know, what a strange thing to say.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，这真是句奇怪的话。

sentences.en: And it was years later when I was doing a lot more work on laughter, I thought, he was right.
sentences.zh: 多年后，当我深入研究笑声时，我才意识到他是对的。

sentences.en: You know, if you can look back on a life where you've shared a lot of laughter with the people
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你回首往事，发现自己曾与周围的人、

sentences.en: around you, with the people that you care about, those are not times wasted.
sentences.zh: 与你在乎的人分享过许多欢笑，那些时光并非虚度。

sentences.en: Those are the good times.
sentences.zh: 那是美好的时光。

sentences.en: Those are the times that really matter.
sentences.zh: 那才是真正重要的时光。

sentences.en: And letting yourself value that rather than thinking that it's a silly or a trivial waste
sentences.zh: 让自己去珍视这些，而不是认为这只是愚蠢或琐碎地浪费

sentences.en: of everyone's time.
sentences.zh: 大家的时间。

sentences.en: You should be spending your time being serious.
sentences.zh: 你本该把时间花在正经事上。

sentences.en: You know, it is worth taking the laughter seriously.
sentences.zh: 要知道，认真对待笑声是值得的。

sentences.en: Today, we take laughter seriously.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们认真对待笑声。

sentences.en: Sophie Scott tells us about the varied shades of laughter, from politeness, to discomfort,
sentences.zh: 苏菲·斯科特将为我们讲述笑声的多重色彩，从礼貌到尴尬，

sentences.en: to delight.
sentences.zh: 再到愉悦。

sentences.zh: 本周《隐藏的大脑》，解读笑声的含义。

sentences.zh: 苏菲·斯科特是伦敦大学学院的神经科学家。

sentences.zh: 她研究笑声，研究大脑如何处理笑声，以及笑声在塑造

sentences.en: social connection.
sentences.zh: 社会联系中扮演的角色。

sentences.zh: 苏菲，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.zh: 苏菲，我想给你播放一段非常奇怪的声音片段。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于笑声的一点是，它更像是一种动物的叫声，而不是

sentences.zh: 任何人类的语言。

sentences.zh: 所以它在人类和其他动物之间可以极其相似。

sentences.zh: 这是一段某人无法控制地大笑的片段。

sentences.en: But it's almost as if another creature has taken this person over.
sentences.zh: 但听起来几乎像是另一个生物占据了这个人的身体。

sentences.en: You know, all the polish and the culture have gone out the window.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有的修养和文明都抛到九霄云外去了。

sentences.en: And you get these strange sounds.
sentences.zh: 你会听到这些奇怪的声音。

sentences.en: These almost animalistic sounds.
sentences.zh: 这些近乎动物般的叫声。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And we actually, in our normal day-to-day behavior, humans have a lot of control over the
sentences.zh: 实际上，在我们日常行为中，人类对我们所做的事情

sentences.en: things that we do and the sounds that we make.
sentences.zh: 和发出的声音有很大的控制力。

sentences.en: And actually, that's one of the things that's unusual about humans.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这也是人类不同寻常的地方之一。

sentences.en: We don't just react flexibly to our environment, but we can modulate how we respond.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅能灵活地对环境做出反应，还能调节我们的反应方式。

sentences.en: And a lot of other animals, particularly for vocalizations, their vocalizations are highly
sentences.zh: 而许多其他动物，特别是发声时，它们的叫声是高度

sentences.en: reflexive.
sentences.zh: 反射性的。

sentences.en: Something happens and they make the sound.
sentences.zh: 发生了什么，它们就发出那种声音。

sentences.en: Something triggers the sound, they make the sound.
sentences.zh: 某种东西触发了声音，它们就发出声音。

sentences.en: And we have a handful of sounds that we make that are from this more kind of reflexive,
sentences.zh: 而我们也有少数几种声音是来自这种更具反射性、

sentences.en: involuntary route.
sentences.zh: 非自愿的途径。

sentences.en: And it can be quite startling when they come out of you.
sentences.zh: 当它们从你口中发出时，可能会相当令人吃惊。

sentences.en: Sounds like weeping, grunting, and gasps of surprise.
sentences.zh: 比如哭泣、咕哝和惊讶的喘息。

sentences.zh: 几周前，我正在做电台录音，出乎意料的是，我们在一个化学实验室里，

sentences.zh: 但发生了一次爆炸。

sentences.en: Anyway, let's just drop it in and see.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们把它放进去看看。

sentences.zh: 在录音带里，我发出了一种非常惊讶的“噢”的声音。

sentences.en: Oh, that was an involuntary vocalization then.
sentences.zh: 噢，那是一种非自愿的发声。

sentences.en: I don't know if you noticed.
sentences.zh: 不知道你有没有注意到。

sentences.en: I was not hoping to make cry.
sentences.zh: 我并不是想哭。

sentences.en: Because I was actually a little bit startled and I thought, oh, that's really irritating.
sentences.zh: 因为我当时确实有点被吓到了，我想，噢，那真烦人。

sentences.en: I wish I hadn't done that.
sentences.zh: 我真希望我没那样做。

sentences.en: But it was completely involuntary.
sentences.zh: 但那是完全非自愿的。

sentences.en: And laughter can be like that as well.
sentences.zh: 笑声也可以是那样的。

sentences.en: It can just feel like it's issuing forth from us.
sentences.zh: 它感觉就像是从我们体内喷涌而出。

sentences.en: And we can make sounds when we're laughing like that, that probably all other things
sentences.zh: 当我们那样笑的时候，我们发出的声音，在其他条件相同的情况下，

sentences.zh: 我们可能更希望不要发出。

sentences.en: It can be extremely, well, very animal.
sentences.zh: 它可以非常，嗯，非常动物性。

sentences.en: And it is animal.
sentences.zh: 它确实是动物性的。

sentences.en: It's linking us to exactly the same way that other animals make sounds.
sentences.zh: 它将我们与其他动物发出声音的方式完全联系在了一起。

sentences.en: Sophie was drawn to studying laughter because she was interested in how humans express emotions.
sentences.zh: 苏菲之所以被吸引去研究笑声，是因为她对人类如何表达情感感兴趣。

sentences.en: Most of the previous work on the subject had focused on visual cues.
sentences.zh: 之前关于这个主题的大多数研究都集中在视觉线索上。

sentences.en: Sophie asked, what about sounds?
sentences.zh: 苏菲问，声音呢？

sentences.en: I got into laughter by being interested in nonverbal vocalization.
sentences.zh: 我开始研究笑声是因为我对非语言发声感兴趣。

sentences.en: So something like me going, oh, when I'm surprised or screaming in terror.
sentences.zh: 比如我惊讶时发出的“噢”，或者恐惧时的尖叫。

sentences.en: And I was working with those because we were interested in how humans recognize emotions.
sentences.zh: 我研究这些是因为我们对人类如何识别情感感兴趣。

sentences.en: And pretty much all the work on that is done with photographs of faces following the beautiful
sentences.zh: 而关于这方面的研究几乎都是基于保罗·埃克曼等人的杰出工作，

sentences.en: work of people like Paul Ekman.
sentences.zh: 使用面部照片进行的。

sentences.en: And I was trying to come up with auditory vocal versions of those.
sentences.zh: 我当时正试图找出这些情感的听觉发声版本。

sentences.en: So I was trying to steer away from emotional speech because the faces didn't have any verbal
sentences.zh: 所以我试图避开情感言语，因为面部表情没有任何语言

sentences.en: content to them.
sentences.zh: 内容。

sentences.en: And it was looking at those and then starting to look at different kinds of expressions that
sentences.zh: 我观察了这些，然后开始研究不同类型的表情，这些表情

sentences.zh: 可能是更积极的情感，也包括像恐惧和愤怒这样的消极情感，这正是

sentences.zh: 引导我研究笑声的原因。

sentences.en: So I never set out to study laughter.
sentences.zh: 所以我从没想过要研究笑声。

sentences.en: I was interested in these nonverbal sounds.
sentences.zh: 我只是对这些非语言声音感兴趣。

sentences.en: And they can be highly involuntary.
sentences.zh: 它们可能是高度非自愿的。

sentences.en: And in fact, when we make them, they are much more like animal calls than they are like speech.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我们发出这些声音时，它们更像动物的叫声，而不是语言。

sentences.en: We don't do any of the fancy detailed movements of the lips and the jaw and the teeth and the
sentences.zh: 我们说话时那种嘴唇、下巴、牙齿和舌头的复杂精细动作，

sentences.zh: 在笑的时候完全没有。

sentences.zh: 事实上，通常嘴巴几乎什么都不做。

sentences.zh: 你可能会做一个面部表情，然后只是把空气从声带

sentences.en: box.

sentences.zh: 有没有证据表明其他动物像人类一样笑？

sentences.zh: 有证据表明其他动物会笑。

sentences.zh: 在其他类人猿身上很容易观察到这一点。

sentences.zh: 事实上，查尔斯·达尔文对此写了很多。

sentences.zh: 你知道，非人类猿类的笑声与人类笑声非常相似。

sentences.zh: 所以如果你听到黑猩猩在笑，那看起来真的很像笑声。

sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到它在视觉上与人类笑声非常、非常相似。

sentences.zh: 但在其他动物身上也描述过类似笑声的发声，

sentences.zh: 它们不是猿类，在进化层面上离我们稍微远一点。

sentences.en: And he was working with rats.
sentences.zh: 他当时在研究老鼠。

sentences.en: other.

sentences.en: with play in apes.

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: when they're playing and when they're being tickled.

sentences.en: ear.

sentences.zh: 因为当老鼠互相玩耍时，笑声发声的作用之一是

sentences.en: The researchers asked the volunteers if they could tell whether the people laughing were friends or strangers.

sentences.en: Why don't you see if you can tell the difference?

sentences.en: Here's one set of three laughs strung together.

sentences.en: And here's another.

sentences.en: If you guessed that the first clip was strangers and the second clip was friends, you're right.

sentences.en: Most people in the study got it right.

sentences.en: People all over the world could hear the difference.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的人都能听出其中的区别。

sentences.en: And it makes sense because we don't laugh with just anybody.
sentences.zh: 这很有道理，因为我们不会随便跟任何人一起笑。

sentences.en: You know, laughter is a very good index of how we feel about the people that we're with.
sentences.zh: 你知道，笑声是衡量我们与身边人关系如何的一个很好的指标。

sentences.en: And it's not like we're laughing or we're not laughing and that's the only difference.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我们只有“笑”或“不笑”这两种区别。

sentences.en: You can have much more kind of performative, you know, if I bump into someone in the street, we both laugh and say we're OK.
sentences.zh: 你可以有更多表演性的笑，比如，如果我在街上撞到某人，我们都会笑笑说没事。

sentences.en: I'm not going to stand there going, that laughter wasn't very intense because I know what it means.
sentences.zh: 我不会站在那里想，那笑声不够强烈，因为我知道它意味着什么。

sentences.en: Like, you know, it was doing its job of sorting out a slightly difficult situation.

sentences.en: Whereas with a friend, the laughter is likely to be much warmer because it needs to be and it can be.
sentences.zh: 而对于朋友，笑声往往会温暖得多，因为这既是必要的，也是可能的。

sentences.en: And it's an index actually of how those friends feel about each other.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是那些朋友对彼此感情如何的一个指标。

sentences.en: So I think it's interesting that we're so alive to it, like we really notice it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为有趣的是，我们对它如此敏感，我们真的会注意到它。

sentences.en: And as I say, I think that's because it's an incredibly important social signal and we recognize its emotional meaning.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我认为这是因为它是一个极其重要的社交信号，我们能识别出它的情感含义。

sentences.en: This emotional meaning is usually positive, but not always.
